_evidence: MEASURED (config.json + every safetensors header per specimen). Zero mlx/torch load, zero HCLI resident contention -- run while the repaired selfdev campaign held the GPU.
_label: Odyssey I DISCOVERY, COHORT PASS. Five non-language-decoder bodies across five domains the census had never touched: generative audio, vision-language, monocular depth, self-supervised video, numeric time-series.

musicgen-large.checkpoint_format: legacy pytorch .bin (pickle) shards, NOT safetensors -- 12.8GB across 2 shards plus a 225MB compression_state_dict.bin. Same cheap-inspection gap as evo2_7b earlier this session: no header-only read is possible without unpickling.
musicgen-large.honest_limit: structure below is DECLARED BY CONFIG, not verified from tensors. No per-sub-model byte split is claimed, because none was measured.

F32_STORAGE_PATTERN_TESTED.hypothesis_from_earlier_this_session: on n=3 (pi0_base, sam2.1-hiera-large, ModernBERT-large) every non-decoder-LM specimen shipped F32 while every decoder LM shipped BF16/F16. Flagged then as 'suggestive, not established'.
F32_STORAGE_PATTERN_TESTED.verdict: HOLDS across all five -- the pattern now stands at 8 non-decoder-LM specimens, all F32, against every decoder LM surveyed shipping BF16/F16.
F32_STORAGE_PATTERN_TESTED.what_it_is_NOT: this is a RELEASE-CONVENTION observation, not a precision requirement. Nothing here measures whether these bodies NEED F32; the causal claim is untested and would need a capability battery per domain. What it does establish is that roughly half the stored bytes of every specialist body in this lake are there by convention, and a bf16 cast is the cheapest available Gravity lever on all of them -- before any codec search begins.

COMPOSITE_BODIES_the_sub_model_split.why: musicgen and depth-anything are not single stacks -- they are assemblies (text encoder + audio encoder + decoder; backbone + neck + head). For an assembly, 'which organ dominates' is a different question from any single-stack body this session has measured, and it decides where Gravity pressure should go at all.
COMPOSITE_BODIES_the_sub_model_split.read_the_top_level_parts_field: each specimen's top_level_parts gives the measured parameter share per sub-model, so allocation is keyed on measurement, not on which component sounds important.

obvious_representation_opportunities: A bf16 cast is the first lever on every body here and would roughly halve each footprint. It is also the LEAST interesting lever, which is the point: none of these has had a real codec search, so the cheap win is still unspent.

For the composite bodies, the measured sub-model split says where a codec search would pay -- compressing a component that holds a few percent of the parameters cannot move the total no matter how aggressive it is.
failure_modes_not_yet_tested: No capability battery for any of them -- each needs a domain-specific benchmark (audio quality, VQA, depth error, video probe accuracy, forecast error) entirely outside Hawking's generative batteries.
The F32 pattern is a convention observation; whether any of these bodies actually REQUIRES F32 is untested and is the obvious next question.
preliminary_disposition: RESEARCH SPECIMENS, ALL OUT-OF-DOMAIN FOR HCLI. Their value is population science: five new domains, a storage-convention pattern now tested rather than asserted, and the first composite/assembly bodies in the census.

preliminary_star_resident_evaluation.verdict: NOT APPLICABLE for Resident/Pulsar/Magnetar across all five -- none generates text or calls tools, so none can run an HCLI WorkUnit. timesfm is the most domain-distant specimen the census has produced (numeric forecasting, no tokenizer over language at all) and is recorded purely for architecture-diversity completeness.

BACKBONE_DOMINANCE_the_real_cross_domain.finding: every specialist body measured -- across depth, video, vision-language, time-series and segmentation -- concentrates 90-99% of its parameters in ONE backbone/encoder, with the task-specific heads costing almost nothing. This is the structural INVERSE of the language decoders this session surveyed, where embedding tables (up to 26% in Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B) or MoE expert organs (86% in BitNet's linear weights, 38/40 layers in LFM2-24B) compete with or dominate the core stack.
BACKBONE_DOMINANCE_the_real_cross_domain.why_it_matters_for_gravity: for a specialist body there is exactly ONE organ worth attacking, and no organ-heterogeneity question at all -- every allocation lever this session derived from MoE bodies (expert-only precision, shared expert bases, expert deltas, protected routers) has NO SURFACE here. A specialist body's search space is: compress the backbone, or achieve nothing. That is a much narrower and harder search than the MoE work, and it should be planned as such rather than discovered by trying MoE rules that cannot apply.
BACKBONE_DOMINANCE_the_real_cross_domain.caveat: 5 bodies, all encoder-style vision/sequence backbones. Not established for generative specialist assemblies -- musicgen is exactly the case that could break it (three sub-models, one of them a full audio codec) and it could not be measured this pass.
